items.title: Phase 0 — Repository baseline
items.body: Safe baseline before production work: analyses stored, work in progress made safe, commits on `release/v1.0.0`.

items.title: Phase 1a — Acceptance tests from the SRS
items.body: Black-box acceptance tests per implemented use case, written from the SRS and the API contract only. Red tests become bug issues. Branch `tests/acceptance`.

items.title: Phase 2 — Functional bugs
items.body: Fix the broken behaviour found in the review and by the acceptance tests.

items.title: Phase 3 — Production foundations
items.body: Tests in CI, hosting and deploy, backups, tooling. Last phase before the first release.

items.title: Phase 4 — Finish mocked basics
items.body: Replace the mocked endpoints of basic features with real ones (profile, likes, contributions, deletes, roles).

items.title: Phase 5 — Complete SRS workflows
items.body: SRS workflows not built for the thesis. Each sub-phase (5a–5e) gets its own plan.

items.title: Phase 6 — Quality and scale
items.body: Architecture clean-ups, performance, accessibility, dependency hygiene.

items.title: Store the project analyses locally
items.body: Code review, SRS coverage, roadmap and decisions log kept locally.

items.title: Make work in progress safe
items.body: Email redirect outside production (`EMAIL_REDIRECT_TO`), group-removal socket event fix, testing seeder `down()` scoped to seeded users, `.gitignore` updates.

items.title: Commit the pending work as Conventional Commits
items.body: Eleven commits on `release/v1.0.0`.

items.title: Branching for the release
items.body: Replaced: instead of fast-forwarding `develop`, work accumulates on `release/v1.0.0` until production. Flow: `release/v1.0.0` → `develop` (pre-production) → `main` (production).

items.title: Testing plan: vocabulary and open questions answered
items.body: Edition and hackathon states, actors, and the questions in testing plan §9 answered.

items.title: Acceptance test infrastructure
items.body: Vitest against the local testing Supabase stack, in-memory fakes for Google Drive and Resend, fixtures named after SRS preconditions, `createApp()` split from `server.js`. See `backend/tests/HELPERS.md`.

items.title: Acceptance tests: UC-002 View editions
items.body:
Black-box acceptance tests written from the SRS (step A2, testing plan §4.1).

Expected behaviour:
- Guest sees announced (`ACTIVE`) editions.
- Guest sees published editions, listed apart from ongoing ones.
- Guest sees `CLOSED` editions, listed together with the ongoing ones.
- Guest does not see not-announced editions.
- With no announced edition, guest gets an empty list.
- List items carry exactly id, state, name, year, short description, logo (+ optional fruit logo); staff also get the Drive link.

Red tests: see the T1 bug issue.

items.title: Acceptance tests: UC-003 Edition details
items.body:
Black-box acceptance tests written from the SRS (step A2, testing plan §4.1).

Expected behaviour:
- Guest gets the full description of an announced edition.
- Published edition: details include its catalogue and a summary of its published fruits (id, main image, title).
- Guest cannot see the details of a not-announced edition (404); unknown id → 404.

Red tests: see the T4 bug issue.

items.title: Acceptance tests: UC-004 View hackathons
items.body:
Black-box acceptance tests written from the SRS (step A2, testing plan §4.1).

Expected behaviour:
- Guests and participants see every announced, closed, ongoing and ended hackathon; never not-announced or internal (private) ones.
- Staff also see not-announced and internal hackathons.
- With none, empty list. No filter in the list.
- Exact item fields per role; authenticated users get `isEnrolled` (participation only; evaluators don't count).

Red tests: see the T8 and T9 bug issues.

items.title: Acceptance tests: UC-006/007 Explore products and product details
items.body:
Black-box acceptance tests written from the SRS (step A2, testing plan §4.1).

Expected behaviour:
- Guest lists the seeds, flowers and fruits of an edition; only published products appear.
- An unpublished seed never appears to a guest or a plain participant (BRU-018).
- Guest gets the details of a published seed, flower and fruit.
- Guest cannot get the details of an unpublished product.

items.title: Acceptance tests: FRQ-001 Authentication
items.body:
Black-box acceptance tests written from the SRS (step A2, testing plan §4.2).

Expected behaviour:
- Valid email + password logs in and returns a working session.
- Wrong password / unknown email is rejected.
- Every restricted operation rejects a guest (`401`).

items.title: Acceptance tests: UC-005a Registration path
items.body:
Black-box acceptance tests written from the SRS (step A2, testing plan §4.2).

Expected behaviour:
- Giving email + full name pre-registers the user and sends an email.
- A pre-registered user can complete registration and then log in.
- Pre-registering an email that is already registered is rejected.

items.title: Acceptance tests: UC-008 View my profile
items.body:
Black-box acceptance tests written from the SRS (step A2, testing plan §4.2).

Expected behaviour:
- Authenticated user gets their own information: email, full name, optional fields if set, and roles.

items.title: Acceptance tests: BRU-001 Multiple roles
items.body:
Black-box acceptance tests written from the SRS (step A2, testing plan §4.2).

Expected behaviour:
- A user who is both facilitator and inspiring scientist can do both kinds of operations.
- Roles returned for that user include both.

items.title: Acceptance tests: BRU-002 Role scope
items.body:
Black-box acceptance tests written from the SRS (step A2, testing plan §4.2).

Expected behaviour:
- Staff roles are global: a facilitator can act on every edition/hackathon.
- Evaluator role is per hackathon: an evaluator of H1 has no evaluator view of H2.
- The same user can be evaluator of two hackathons.
- Inspiring scientist role is per edition: scientist of E1 cannot create seeds in E2.

items.title: Acceptance tests: UC-005 Join a hackathon
items.body:
Black-box acceptance tests written from the SRS (step A3, testing plan §4.3).

Expected behaviour:
- Participant joins an announced, upcoming hackathon giving roles and reasons → enrolled; roles and reason stored.
- Joining a hackathon that is not announced, closed, ongoing or ended is rejected.
- Joining twice doesn't create a second enrolment.
- After joining, UC-004 marks that hackathon as enrolled for the user.

items.title: Acceptance tests: UC-042 View enrolled users
items.body:
Black-box acceptance tests written from the SRS (step A3, testing plan §4.3).

Expected behaviour:
- Facilitator gets the list of enrolled participants; empty list when none.
- Participant / guest rejected.

items.title: Acceptance tests: UC-035 Invite scientists to an edition
items.body:
Black-box acceptance tests written from the SRS (step A3, testing plan §4.4).

Expected behaviour:
- Facilitator invites an existing user → that user becomes inspiring scientist of the edition.
- Facilitator invites an unknown email → pre-registration + invitation email.
- Inviting to a not-yet-public edition works (BRU-033); to a closed edition is rejected (BRU-008).
- Participant rejected.

items.title: Acceptance tests: UC-033 Manage scientist invitations
items.body:
Black-box acceptance tests written from the SRS (step A3, testing plan §4.4).

Expected behaviour:
- Designer sees the editions list for a scientist, marked invited / not invited; adds and removes editions.
- Facilitator cannot manage these invitations (designer-only).
- Removing an edition where the scientist already created a seed is cancelled (BRU-007).
- Adding a closed edition is cancelled (BRU-008, BRU-044).
- Participant rejected.

items.title: Acceptance tests: UC-018 View collaborating editions
items.body:
Black-box acceptance tests written from the SRS (step A3, testing plan §4.4).

Expected behaviour:
- Scientist sees exactly the editions they were invited to, with incoming / ongoing / past distinguished.
- A user who is not a scientist gets an empty list or is rejected.

items.title: Acceptance tests: UC-019 My seeds of an edition
items.body:
Black-box acceptance tests written from the SRS (step A3, testing plan §4.4).

Expected behaviour:
- Scientist gets the seeds they created or collaborate on in that edition; not other scientists' seeds.
- Empty list when none.

items.title: Acceptance tests: UC-020 Create a seed
items.body:
Black-box acceptance tests written from the SRS (step A3, testing plan §4.4).

Expected behaviour:
- Invited scientist creates a seed → in progress, belongs to that edition, creator stored as original author.
- An empty seed template document is generated from the edition's master template.
- Scientist not invited to that edition is rejected; several seeds per scientist allowed (BRU-034).
- Plain participant rejected. The new seed is not publicly visible (BRU-018).

items.title: Acceptance tests: UC-024 Fill out seed information
items.body:
Black-box acceptance tests written from the SRS (step A3, testing plan §4.4).

Expected behaviour:
- Author updates the seed fields → persisted; optional video, presentation and podcast links stored.
- Another scientist who is not author or collaborator is rejected.
- Once delivered, the scientist can no longer edit it (BRU-017).

items.title: Acceptance tests: UC-029 Create edition
items.body:
Black-box acceptance tests written from the SRS (step A4, testing plan §4.5).

Expected behaviour:
- Designer creates an edition with name, year, descriptions, logo → exists and is not announced.
- An empty seed master template is generated.
- Facilitator, participant and guest cannot create an edition.

items.title: Acceptance tests: UC-031 Announce edition
items.body:
Black-box acceptance tests written from the SRS (step A4, testing plan §4.5).

Expected behaviour:
- Designer announces a fully specified edition → guests now see it.
- Missing name, year, short or long description → cancelled (BRU-004), one test per field.
- Already announced → rejected. Facilitator / participant rejected.

items.title: Acceptance tests: UC-036 Modify edition
items.body:
Black-box acceptance tests written from the SRS (step A4, testing plan §4.5).

Expected behaviour:
- Facilitator modifies edition information → persisted.
- A `CLOSED` edition's descriptions can still be edited; a `PUBLISHED` edition can't be edited at all.
- After announcement, changes to name and year are not applied; other changes are (BRU-044).
- Participant rejected.

items.title: Acceptance tests: UC-037 Create hackathon
items.body:
Black-box acceptance tests written from the SRS (step A4, testing plan §4.6).

Expected behaviour:
- Facilitator creates a hackathon under a not-closed edition → not announced, linked to the edition.
- An empty flower master template is generated. Closed edition → rejected (BRU-009).
- On-site / hybrid stores a location; online / hybrid stores a meet link, which is optional at creation.
- Participant rejected.

items.title: Acceptance tests: UC-038 Modify hackathon
items.body:
Black-box acceptance tests written from the SRS (step A4, testing plan §4.6).

Expected behaviour:
- Facilitator modifies information → persisted.
- After announcement, changes to dates, type and edition are not applied (BRU-038).
- Evaluators and seeds can change only before start (BRU-012, BRU-038).
- Seeds must be published and from the parent edition (BRU-039).

items.title: Acceptance tests: UC-041 Announce hackathon
items.body:
Black-box acceptance tests written from the SRS (step A4, testing plan §4.6).

Expected behaviour:
- Facilitator announces a complete hackathon whose edition is announced → guests see it and users can join.
- Parent edition not announced → cancelled (BRU-010).
- Incomplete information → cancelled, one test per attribute; meet link never required to announce.
- Participant rejected.

items.title: Acceptance tests: UC-043 Close hackathon
items.body:
Black-box acceptance tests written from the SRS (step A4, testing plan §4.6).

Expected behaviour:
- Facilitator closes an announced hackathon with participants → closed; new joins rejected.
- No enrolled participants → cancelled. Participant rejected.

items.title: Acceptance tests: UC-044 Start hackathon
items.body:
Black-box acceptance tests written from the SRS (step A4, testing plan §4.6).

Expected behaviour:
- Closed hackathon with evaluators, seeds, start date ≤ today and ≥ 1 participant → started.
- No evaluators / no seeds / future start date / no participants → rejected.
- Online or hybrid without a meet link → rejected; on-site without one → allowed.
- Participant rejected.

items.title: Acceptance tests: UC-047 Enter ongoing hackathon
items.body:
Black-box acceptance tests written from the SRS (step A5, testing plan §4.7).

Expected behaviour:
- Participant marked as assisting (by the facilitator) can open the ongoing hackathon and gets the current phase.
- A participant cannot mark their own or anyone's assistance.
- Not-enrolled user or hackathon not ongoing → cannot enter (BRU-048).
- Admins, facilitators and the hackathon's evaluators can enter.

items.title: Acceptance tests: UC-057 Assistance control
items.body:
Black-box acceptance tests written from the SRS (step A5, testing plan §4.7).

Expected behaviour:
- Facilitator lists assisting participants; adds and removes one manually → reflected.
- Participant cannot change someone else's assistance.

items.title: Acceptance tests: UC-058 Create exploring groups
items.body:
Black-box acceptance tests written from the SRS (step A5, testing plan §4.7).

Expected behaviour:
- Facilitator creates one group per seed and assigns assisting participants.
- Exactly one group voice per group (BRU-032); one group per participant (BRU-041).
- Non-assisting participants are not grouped; can't move on while someone has no group or a group has no voice.
- Participant / evaluator cannot create groups.

items.title: Acceptance tests: UC-048 Develop conceptual map
items.body:
Black-box acceptance tests written from the SRS (step A5, testing plan §4.7).

Expected behaviour:
- Two members of the same group connected by socket: a change from one reaches the other.
- The map content is stored: after everyone disconnects, reading it returns the last content (IRQ-009).
- After delivery, member edits are not applied (BRU-040).

items.title: Acceptance tests: UC-049 Submit conceptual map
items.body:
Black-box acceptance tests written from the SRS (step A5, testing plan §4.7).

Expected behaviour:
- Group voice delivers → map delivered.
- Non-voice member or non-member rejected (BRU-024); delivering twice rejected.

items.title: Acceptance tests: UC-059 Follow up group work
items.body:
Black-box acceptance tests written from the SRS (step A5, testing plan §4.7).

Expected behaviour:
- Facilitator lists groups with each map's progress and delivery status.
- Facilitator reopens a delivered map → editable, must be delivered again; reopening an open map rejected; participants cannot reopen.

items.title: Acceptance tests: UC-060/051 Group presentations
items.body:
Black-box acceptance tests written from the SRS (step A5, testing plan §4.7).

Expected behaviour:
- Facilitator sets the presenting group → everyone in the hackathon room receives it.
- The group voice's group receives "your turn".
- The current presenting group is stored: a client that connects later gets it.

items.title: Acceptance tests: UC-050/052 Rate seeds and submit ratings
items.body:
Black-box acceptance tests written from the SRS (step A5, testing plan §4.7).

Expected behaviour:
- Participant rates a presented seed 1–5; values outside 1–5 rejected; own group's seed allowed (BRU-023).
- Submitting before rating all presented seeds is rejected; after submitting, ratings are locked (BRU-042).
- Ratings survive a server restart (IRQ-007).
- Facilitator receives the submitted ratings.

items.title: Acceptance tests: UC-061 Create co-creation teams
items.body:
Black-box acceptance tests written from the SRS (step A5, testing plan §4.8).

Expected behaviour:
- Only after group presentations have ended.
- Facilitator creates teams per seed with one speaker each; one team per participant (BRU-032, BRU-041).
- Can't move on while someone has no team or a team has no speaker.
- Facilitator sees ratings and disciplines while forming teams.

items.title: Acceptance tests: UC-053 Develop flower
items.body:
Black-box acceptance tests written from the SRS (step A5, testing plan §4.8).

Expected behaviour:
- Team member sees the seed, its conceptual maps and the flower template link.
- Each team gets its own flower template from the hackathon's master template.

items.title: Acceptance tests: UC-054 Submit flower
items.body:
Black-box acceptance tests written from the SRS (step A5, testing plan §4.8).

Expected behaviour:
- Team speaker delivers → flower delivered.
- Non-speaker or non-member rejected; delivering twice rejected.
- After delivery, members can't edit the flower information (BRU-036).

items.title: Acceptance tests: UC-062 Follow up team work
items.body:
Black-box acceptance tests written from the SRS (step A5, testing plan §4.8).

Expected behaviour:
- Facilitator lists teams with each flower's progress and delivery status.
- Facilitator reopens a delivered flower; reopening an open one rejected; participants cannot reopen.

items.title: Acceptance tests: UC-063/055/056 Team presentations
items.body:
Black-box acceptance tests written from the SRS (step A5, testing plan §4.8).

Expected behaviour:
- Facilitator sets the presenting team → participants and evaluators receive it with a flower and seed summary.
- The team speaker's team receives "your turn".
- The current presenting team is stored.

items.title: Acceptance tests: UC-064 Fill out rubric
items.body:
Black-box acceptance tests written from the SRS (step A5, testing plan §4.8).

Expected behaviour:
- One empty rubric exists per evaluator × flower once flowers are delivered.
- Evaluator gets the link to their own rubric for a chosen team.

items.title: Acceptance tests: UC-066 View hackathon management process
items.body:
Black-box acceptance tests written from the SRS (step A5, testing plan §4.8).

Expected behaviour:
- Facilitator and evaluator see assisting participants, groups or teams, maps or flowers.
- Evaluator cannot perform any management action (BRU-025).
- Participant cannot see the management view.

items.title: Acceptance tests: UC-067 End hackathon
items.body:
Black-box acceptance tests written from the SRS (step A5, testing plan §4.8).

Expected behaviour:
- Facilitator ends the hackathon after team presentations → it appears as past.

items.title: Acceptance tests: full hackathon journey
items.body: One test through the API and sockets only: edition created → announced → scientist invited → seed → hackathon → announced → participants join → closed → started → groups → maps → presentations + ratings → teams → flowers → presentations → rubrics → ended. Shows the first broken step. Step A6, testing plan §4.9.

items.title: Acceptance tests: role-based access matrix
items.body: One table-driven test: every restricted operation × {guest, participant, scientist of another edition, evaluator, facilitator} → allowed or rejected as the actor of its use case says. Plus the requirements status report generated from the test run. Step A6, testing plan §4.10 and §7.

items.title: CI workflow for lint, build and tests
items.body: Root `.github/workflows/ci.yml`: lint, build, backend acceptance tests, Playwright chromium. While Phase 2 is open the acceptance job is informative; anything green before is blocking. Step A7.

items.title: Playwright UI acceptance tests
items.body: Guest browsing, login + profile, joining a hackathon, staff creating and announcing, group management, shared conceptual map in two browsers. Step A8, testing plan §5.

items.title: Acceptance baseline run and report
items.body: Full run, every red test logged as a finding, report reviewed. Step A9.

items.title: Editions list: unauthorised state filter returns 200 instead of 401/403
items.body:
`GET /editions?state=PLANNED` as a guest returns `200` instead of `401`, and as a participant `200` instead of `403`. The list itself is correct (no planned editions), only the status is wrong.

Red tests: `editionsList.test.js` "guest asking…unauthorised", "participant asking…forbidden".

items.title: Edition details: fruit summary fields don't match the contract
items.body:
Fruit summary items in a published edition's details should be exactly `id`, `mainImage`, `title`. `mainImage` is missing and `seed`/`flower` are extra.

Red tests: `editionDetails.test.js` fruit main image / fruit fields.

items.title: Hackathons list: items send `description` instead of `shortDescription`
items.body:
List items carry `description`; the contract field is `shortDescription` (IRQ-006 short description).

Red tests: `hackathonsList.test.js` "guest list items carry every required field", and the exact-shape tests.

items.title: Hackathons list: guests get an `isEnrolled` field
items.body:
Guest items carry `isEnrolled: false`. Only authenticated users should get `isEnrolled`.

Red tests: `hackathonsList.test.js` "guest items carry no isEnrolled", and the guest exact-shape test.

items.title: Hackathon state transitions always fail
items.body: Advancing a hackathon PLANNED → OPEN → CLOSED always returns 400, which blocks announcing, closing and starting hackathons. The state classes don't return the shape the caller expects. Also fix the log message that prints the phase instead of the state.

items.title: Meet link required for on-site hackathons
items.body: The on-site check is inverted: the meet link is demanded for on-site hackathons instead of online/hybrid ones.

items.title: Staff role scope not applied in some queries
items.body: The internal staff role object isn't the same as `ROLES.STAFF`, so role-keyed scope maps fall back to the default scope. Effects: next-phase lookup fails on planned hackathons, edition-name uniqueness ignores unpublished editions. Key the maps by role name.

items.title: An evaluator can only evaluate one hackathon
items.body: The database keeps a unique index on the evaluator's user profile, while the model expects uniqueness per (user, hackathon). Contradicts BRU-002. Needs a migration.

items.title: Seed ratings are lost on restart
items.body: Ratings live only in process memory. IRQ-007 requires storing them, and the free hosting plan restarts the server when idle. Add a ratings table, persist from the socket handlers, lock after submit (BRU-042).

items.title: Model and migration drift
items.body: Seed state enum/default, `Edition.name` uniqueness and `UserProfile.id` default exist only in the models; the new-user trigger never sets `authId`; missing FK indexes. Fix with migrations.

items.title: Frontend socket listeners are never removed
items.body: No `socket.off` cleanups, so handlers accumulate; stale closures in `HackathonManagement`. Add cleanups and functional `setState`.

items.title: Small robustness fixes
items.body:
- Null guards in auth and in the custom error handler
- Email validation pattern in the API spec is too lenient
- `joinMeHackathon` nests a second `withController`
- `EditionActionButton` buttons only log
- `Carousel` crashes while loading

items.title: Regression tests for the Phase 1–2 fixes
items.body: Every fix in Phases 1–2 keeps its acceptance test green in CI.

items.title: Playwright smoke setup
items.body: `baseURL` and `webServer` in the Playwright config; delete the template spec.

items.title: Single root CI workflow
items.body: Root workflow replaces `frontend/.github`; required checks on `develop` and `main`.

items.title: Deploy configuration and environment examples
items.body: Hosting as in the memoir §4.6: Netlify (frontend), Render web service (backend + Socket.IO), Supabase Cloud. Pre-production = `develop`, production = `main`. `.env.example` per package; `BACKEND_URL` in production env.

items.title: Database backups and restore drill (NFRQ-017)
items.body: The Supabase free plan has no backups: scheduled `pg_dump` stored privately (e.g. the Drive workspace), plus a tested restore.

items.title: Tooling: Node version, root scripts, README
items.body: `engines` / `.nvmrc`, `concurrently` for root scripts, root README (NFRQ-003).

items.title: Idempotent seeders and reversible migrations
items.body: Seeders can be re-run safely; fix broken migration `down()`s (document, never rename applied migrations).

items.title: Project documentation structure
items.body: Move the project docs to `docs/project/` (index and status, decisions, roadmap, SRS coverage, product owner clarifications, testing plan and briefs, tools) and track the Claude Code agent, skills and rules, so each fact is kept once. Security material stays private.

items.title: Edit and view profiles (UC-009, UC-010, FRQ-004)
items.body: Replace the mocks; public/private visibility per field.

items.title: Contributions and likes (UC-012, UC-014–016)
items.body: Replace the mocked contributions and like/unlike endpoints.

items.title: Withdraw from a hackathon (UC-011)
items.body: New endpoint and UI (BRU-020, FRQ-006).

items.title: Delete edition and hackathon (UC-030, UC-045)
items.body: With BRU-003/013 checks and FRQ-012 notification.

items.title: Role management and user deletion (UC-027, UC-028)
items.body: FRQ-002 role management; delete user with data export (NFRQ-009).

items.title: Frontend auth context and protected routes
items.body: `AuthContext`, `<ProtectedRoute role>`, `useFetcher` loading state, `response.ok`, AbortController.

items.title: Phase 5a — Seed lifecycle
items.body: Deliver / review / reopen (UC-025/039/040/080), delete (UC-026), collaboration invitations with status (UC-021–023), scientist applications (UC-017), notes (UC-013). Gets its own plan when it starts.

items.title: Phase 5b — Edition and hackathon rules
items.body: Close edition (UC-032), remaining business rules in transitions, rubrics with submit/lock and the end condition (UC-065/067). Gets its own plan when it starts.

items.title: Phase 5c — Suggested groups and teams
items.body: FRQ-023/024 as pure service functions feeding the existing drag-and-drop UI. Gets its own plan when it starts.

items.title: Phase 5d — Post-hackathon stage
items.body: Funding, continue/leave, fruit CRUD and its review/publish flow, curator's vision, exhibition images, deadlines, follow-up, evaluation results, catalogue upload (UC-068–081). Gets its own plan when it starts.

items.title: Phase 5e — Notifications
items.body: `notify(event, recipients, data)` with EJS templates after commit; FRQ-005–015; retry/outbox table. Gets its own plan when it starts.

items.title: Layering clean-up
items.body: Repositories own all model access; break the Roles import cycle; states emit events instead of importing sockets.

items.title: Performance: Drive lookups, pagination, role cache
items.body: Batch/cache Drive image lookups, paginate lists, cache roles per request.

items.title: Durable diagrams and multi-instance sockets
items.body: Persist diagram state periodically; plan the socket.io Redis adapter (NFRQ-005/010).

items.title: Frontend quality: dedupe, a11y, lazy routes, i18n
items.body: Dedupe Group/Team and Edition/Hackathon components; accessibility + `eslint-plugin-jsx-a11y` (NFRQ-001/016); lazy routes; strings module (NFRQ-011).

items.title: Dependency hygiene
items.body: Remove unused deps (`zod`, `@google-cloud/local-auth`, `reactflow`, `dotenv`); `AsyncLocalStorage` instead of `cls-hooked`; upgrade `googleapis`.
